approved: Defence Legislation Amendment (Woomera Prohibited Area) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would open the Woomera Prohibited Area to mining and other non-defence activities while keeping Defence as the main user.
It would create a permit system for non-defence access, divide the area into three zones and set up a coordination office and an advisory board.
New users would be barred from the red zone except for a geological survey by the South Australian Government with Commonwealth agencies.
Authorise the Minister for Defence to make rules defining the Woomera Prohibited Area and its zones.
Create a permit system for non-defence access and use of the area.
Introduce offences and penalties for entering without permission or breaking a permit condition.
Provide for compensation when property is acquired on other than just terms under the new Part VIB.
Confirm that compensation remains available for loss or damage caused by Defence testing.
Allow the Rules to limit the Commonwealth's liability for breach of duty of care in the testing area.
Non-defence users such as miners, pastoralists, Indigenous groups and railway operators, as well as the Defence portfolio and the South Australian Government.

Introduced the Defence Legislation Amendment (Woomera Prohibited Area) Bill 2014 implementing the Hawke review's coexistence model, noting South Australia's government estimates about $35 billion in minerals could be exploited from the 124,000 square kilometre area over the next decade, and that the changes would save resource companies about $690,000 in administrative costs over 10 years.

Supported the Defence Legislation Amendment (Woomera Prohibited Area) Bill 2014, noting the Hawke review made 65 recommendations for a coexistence model dividing the 127,000 square kilometre area into red, amber and green zones, with the excluded red zone covering about eight per cent and the accessible green zone about 75 per cent.

Argued that the Woomera Prohibited Area bill offers a path to revive South Australia's struggling economy, noting the state's representation fell from 12 to 11 federal seats in 2004, and said a proposed Eyre Peninsula port could handle 20 million tonnes of iron ore a year from the region.

Summed up the Defence Legislation Amendment (Woomera Prohibited Area) Bill 2014, which implements the Hawke review's recommendations to let Defence and non-Defence users share the Woomera rocket range, longer than the British Isles, under a negotiated framework of access and safety protections.
